title: Expansion of the geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate synthase gene family underlies the evolution of terpenoid biosynthesis in termites
experiments_summary: The study employed multiple experimental and computational approaches: (1) Chemical profiling: GC-MS and GC×GC-MS analyses of hexane body washes from castes of Embiratermes neotenicus and Nasutitermes takasagoensis; chiral GC-FID for enantiomer determination of monoterpenes (pinene, limonene) and sesquiterpenes (nerolidol); preparative GC coupled with 1H/13C NMR (including 2D COSY, HSQC, HMBC, ROESY) for structural elucidation of unknown polycyclic diterpenes. (2) Genome and transcriptome sequencing and assembly: Oxford Nanopore long-read sequencing and Illumina RNA-seq for E. neotenicus genome assembly (Flye, Pilon polishing, BRAKER annotation); de novo transcriptome assemblies for E. neotenicus, Stylotermes halumicus, and additional termite species using rnaSPAdes. (3) Gene identification and phylogenetics: BLAST-based searches for FPPS, GGPPS, FPPS-like, and GGPPS-like sequences across termite genomes and transcriptomes; manual annotation of GGPPS-like loci using IGV; maximum-likelihood phylogenetic reconstruction with IQ-TREE2 across diverse termite and insect taxa; sequence logo generation for FARM/SARM motifs using ggseqlogo. (4) Transposable element analysis: Genome-wide TE prediction using the EDTA pipeline (RepeatModeler + RepeatMasker); TE density enrichment analyses in 100 kb windows around GGPPS-like loci versus random permutations and protein-coding gene regions using BEDtools; TE family representation analysis and identification of a specific CACTA TIR transposon (TE_00000081) in GGPPS-like loci. (5) Differential gene expression and proteomics: RNA-seq mapping (STAR aligner), TPM normalization, and differential expression analysis (DESeq2, edgeR) comparing queens vs. nymphs in E. neotenicus; label-free quantitative (LFQ) mass spectrometry on nymph and queen tissue fractions analyzed by nano-LC on an Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid, with data processed in MaxQuant and Perseus. (6) Functional characterization of recombinant proteins: Heterologous expression of codon-optimized genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain JWY501 (engineered to accumulate GGPP) with galactose induction; expression of His-tagged proteins in E. coli Lemo21(DE3) with auto-induction medium and purification by Ni-affinity chromatography (HisTrap); in vitro TPS assays using GPP, FPP, or GGPP as substrates with SPME fiber headspace sampling and GC-MS analysis; in vitro IDS assays using IPP combined with DMAPP, GPP, or FPP, with pyrophosphate products analyzed by HPLC-Orbitrap MS (negative mode ESI); site-directed mutagenesis (T152I substitution in NtGGPPS6) to probe the role of Thr152 in cyclization and enantioselectivity. (7) Structural modeling and motif analysis: AlphaFold3 modeling of EneoC, EneoE, NtGGPPS6, ancestral node 2 sequence; homology modeling of EneoJ and NtGGPPS7 using Modeller with human GGPPS structure (PDB: 2Q80) as template; active site cavity identification using KVFinder-web; structural alignment and visualization in UCSF ChimeraX; MEME-based identification of insect GGPPS motifs (IGMs). (8) Selection analysis: HyPhy RELAX for clade-wide selection intensity differences between canonical GGPPS and GGPPS-like branches; HyPhy aBSREL for episodic diversifying selection on individual branches; PAML branch-site tests (CODEML) with Bayes Empirical Bayes method for identifying positively selected codon sites; ancestral sequence reconstruction using PAML.
